thread:
mike: Quick heads-up on a packing + apply gating idea for airgapped hotpatches. Ran into lots of IO chatter with thousands of tiny model shards.

anita: curious, what's the ask?

mike: two options: (A) keep streaming many tiny files as-is; or (B) pack shards into chunked archives that stream as a few large blobs and unpack locally. Both have tradeoffs.

kai: packing reduces etcd/status pressure and fewer fs ops during transfer. But unpacking is CPU-heavy and we lose per-shard streaming visibility.

doug: downside: if unpack step fails mid-way, rollback surface is bigger. Need strong integrity checks + resumable unpack.

leah: proposal: hybrid flow: pack by "transfer groups" (e.g., per-component or per-tier). Sidecar streams group blobs; each group is checkpointed with a manifest. Unpack happens into temp dir -> verify checksums -> atomically swap.

mike: exactly. Transfer groups shrink the number of status updates, but we still preserve component-level verification after unpack.

anita: how do we signal progress? Group-level status alone hides fine-grained liveness for canaries.

kai: sidecar should emit two-level status: group {id, bytes_received, state} and per-component verification events after unpack. Batch both into aggregated status writes.

doug: make batching window tunable; default 2s. Add a max_status_events_per_minute operator knob to protect etcd.

leah: activation gating idea: require TOP tier components to be VERIFIED before activating runtime. NORMAL tiers can be in IMPORTING state; controller tracks compatibility matrix to ensure runtime and models match.

mike: compatibility check must be cheap. Use component-compat labels (semantic ids) and reject TOP activation if model_semver mismatch with runtime_semver.

anita: what about canary / progressive unpack? Could unpack only TOP groups first, activate, then continue unpacking rest. That reduces downtime for critical patches.

kai: that works but increases complexity of bundle layout. Builder must demarcate groups and specify priority. We'll need a small manifest extension.

doug: security: signed manifests must include group digests. Validators verify signature before any unpack. If signature invalid, fail fast.

leah: we should also support resumable unpack: record last-complete-chunk index per-group in sidecar status so restarts pick up where they left off.

mike: testing matrix: airgapped node with slow disk, simulated FD locks, and heavy CPU for decompression. Measure: time-to-first-TOP-ready, bytes-on-wire, status-write-rate, etcd_ops/sec.

anita: Dedicated question: for Dedicated with reserved GPU pools, we may keep model shards on a shared NFS or object-store accessible to worker nodes. Packing/unpacking semantics differ. Consider a mode where pack is uploaded to object-store and workers fetch unpacked objects locally.

kai: add operator mode: PACKING=always|never|auto. Auto picks pack when total shard count > threshold. Threshold tunable per-tenant.

doug: retro on rollback: if TOP activates and later probes fail, we need a rollback that can remove swapped-in dirs safely while other groups are mid-unpack. We'll implement a three-way state: ACTIVE, ROLLING_BACK, CLEANUP. Cleanup has a garbage-collection phase with retention window.

leah: UX: status keys exposed in BundleApplyStatus: group_statuses (list-of-strings summarized), component_verifications (list-of-strings summarized), activation_window_expires_at (string timestamp). Keep the spec unchanged.

mike: operation knobs: batching_window_ms, max_status_per_sec, pack_threshold_shard_count, canary_window_ms. Defaults sensible.

anita: agree. Also add metrics: pack_rate, unpack_cpu_seconds, percent_fastpath_TOP_ready.

kai: follow-up: RFC to define bundle manifest group schema, sidecar status contract, and controller activation state machine. I can draft sequence diagrams for group-stream -> unpack -> verify -> swap -> probe -> commit.

doug: can we do a small POC with 3 groups (TOP, NORMAL, DEFERRED) and 2k tiny shards to compare streaming vs pack?

mike: yep. assign me and kai. deploy-bot: Created task INF-2099: pack-group-poc (assignees: mike,kai) <https://tracker.redwood.local/browse/INF-2099>

leah: cool. I'll log test scenarios and help with Dedicated permutations.

mike: thanks. I'll post early perf numbers in this thread.
